name: dsh-professor-pane
description: The right pane of the DeepSeek Harness as the professor's visualization pane: course outline, class progress, the inbox, and the resolved preferences, switched by a button bar.

comments.client: `lib/client.js` is HAND-WRITTEN in the module-loader's registration form (`window.__ModuleLoader__.load({id, factory})`) rather than produced by tsdown, and there is deliberately no build step. Every shipped client half in node_modules/@deepseek-ai is that same shape, so the format is a contract rather than a private artefact, and one file of plain ES2020 with React.createElement is cheaper to keep true than a bundler config this project would otherwise not have. If this grows past a few hundred lines, add the bundler then.
comments.inject: `dsh.client.inject` names PACKAGES whose client halves must be live first, not services. ui-layout because the `details` seat is declared inside its AppFrame children table and does not exist until that entry mounts; ui-conversation because the header-action seat this pane's opener sits in is declared by its session header; client-runtime for `slots` and `sessions`. The service names this plugin injects are the `inject` export in index.js and lib/client.js.
comments.dependency: This reads the course model through `@ainar/core/src/**` — the package in ainar-node/, imported as TypeScript because Node strips types on import. Until 2026-09-16 it read `dsh-ainar-course-model/server/**`, a second compiled copy of the same model; the pane and the course-model plugin now import the one source, so a change to the model reaches both without anyone keeping two trees in step. `@ainar/core` is a dependency of the PROJECT rather than of this package, for the reason the course model's package.json gives: pnpm cannot resolve a file: spec whose absolute path contains a space, and this checkout lives under a home directory that has one. Node resolution finds it from the dsh installation's node_modules either way.
